problem: Directly combining a foundation model (GPT-4o) with humanoid skill libraries gives poor robustness and efficiency: bipedal locomotion is unstable and needs frequent closed-loop correction, the FM has weak 3D scene understanding and high latency, and navigation often ends in poses unsuitable for manipulation.
motivation: Humanoids need autonomous agents for long-horizon tasks mixing navigation and manipulation, but wheeled or quadruped agent recipes do not transfer because of locomotion instability. The observation is that a slow, cloud-based FM cannot serve as the real-time controller, so a lightweight onboard VLM is needed between the FM and the skills to ground plans, run fast closed-loop navigation and fix the pose for manipulation.
key_idea: Insert a lightweight onboard VLM-based Connector between a GPT-4o planner and a modular locomotion/manipulation skill library to ground language plans, run fast closed-loop visual navigation, and adjust pose before manipulation.
insight: The Connector is the critical component: without it GPT-4o alone fails to reach distant targets (0/5 navigation, 0.00 on Fetch-bottle, Deliver-basket and Prepare-coffee) because of poor direction and depth estimation, and it is also much slower (2.3 vs 9.6 cm/s). The pose-adjustment ablation shows manipulation success depends on where navigation ends (e.g., Grasp-coffee 1/5 to 4/5), and the active-camera ablation shows no fixed pitch works for both navigation and manipulation.
method: Modular Skill Library: RL-trained goal-conditioned locomotion policy driven by joystick commands (50 Hz, sim-to-real, Isaac Gym), plus head skills (tilt/turn), plus per-task ACT manipulation skills learned from VisionPro teleoperation (50-200 trajectories each).
Foundation Model planner: Cradle-style GPT-4o agent with reasoning, success detection (self-reflection) and skill planning from image observations.

Connector VLM: VideoLLaMA2 (SigLIP encoder) fine-tuned on annotated first-person indoor images for bounding-box detection, yes/no and description, and skill prediction; about 1 s inference on the onboard Jetson AGX.
Grounded skill planning: the VLM converts the FM's language plan into feasible skills (e.g., 'grasp cup' becomes move_towards(table) when far away) and signals success back to the FM.

Visual navigation composites: move_towards uses detected bounding box plus stereo depth to choose locomotion commands and sidestep obstacles; search_for combines turning with active head movement when the target is not visible.
Pose adjustment: the VLM predicts the optimal alignment direction, and a composite head-turn plus forward-move skill approaches the object along an arc to give a good initial state for manipulation.
Active vision: a 2-DoF neck with a binocular camera is used to look forward for navigation and downward for tabletop manipulation.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o (frozen) planner + VideoLLaMA2 VLM Connector (fine-tuned) + RL locomotion policy + ACT manipulation policies (ResNet-50, trained per skill)
setting.training_data: Connector: 300K filtered general visual-grounding samples, then 3,177 self-collected first-person office images (about 38K VLU samples plus 771 action-planning samples); ACT skills: 25-200 teleoperated trajectories per skill; locomotion: RL in simulation
setting.observation: binocular RGB (ZED-mini on an actuated neck) with synthetic depth plus proprioception/IMU
setting.action_space: skill-level commands (joystick-based locomotion skills, head skills, manipulation skills) executed as joint-position targets for PD control
setting.simulator: Isaac Gym for locomotion training only; evaluation in the real world
setting.privileged: semantic map of the office given in the FM prompts (place names and current location); otherwise none

numbers.extra: real robot, 20x20 m office; trials are 5 per subprocess (per-task rate as printed)

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmark is used; all results are real-world trials with small counts (5 per setting). Efficiency: Being-0 9.6 cm/s and 5/5 success vs w/o Connector 2.3 cm/s and 0/5 (4.2x speed).
results: On five real-world long-horizon tasks Being-0 reaches completion rates of 0.75-0.90 (average 84.4%), while the GPT-4o-only variant without the Connector scores 0.00 on three tasks and 0.33 on Deliver-coffee. Navigation is 4.2x faster with the Connector and the active camera achieves 5/5 on all navigation and manipulation tests where fixed cameras fail on one or the other.
limitations: Only flat-ground locomotion (no crouching, sitting, jumping or stairs).
Still relies on the slow cloud GPT-4o for high-level decisions.
Evaluated only in one office environment with few trials (5 per setting) and no standardized benchmark; the FM prompt uses a semantic map.
